Cause established mechanically, not guessed: review.oracle.S1.json records outcome accepted at commit ac9cd2aae51a0c0678a80a3f0a5ad9c93523cf35 with content digest 5a29e8ea...68a3; the next commit ab6fe1b (the S2 oracle) added to the same three S1-declared oracle/support files - argv 'git diff --stat ac9cd2a..0394a2a -- crates/foundry-acceptance/' exit 0 shows steps/feature_instance_integration_setup.rs +36, support/instance_integration_setup.rs +47, tests/features/instance-integration-setup.feature +28/-4 - and review.oracle.S2.json records accepted at ab6fe1b with digest 394a8779...377a. argv 'git diff --stat ab6fe1b..0394a2a -- crates/foundry-acceptance/' exit 0 prints nothing, so the craft commit 0394a2a changed no test byte: the oracle bytes under review are exactly those the S2 oracle review approved, and only the S1 record is stale against the additions S2 made to the shared files. Nothing in the candidate was edited to work around this; the prerequisite is a fresh independent S1 oracle approval at 0394a2a limited to that delta (owner: the independent oracle reviewer), after which this close can be retried unchanged. findings.obligation: US-IIS-04 Technical Notes in docs/feature/instance-integration-setup/discuss/user-stories.md:698-700 ('NavContext.is_instance_admin is already read on every page, so this adds no query'), the S1 design record for matrix_setup.rs:281 ('it keeps doing so through the Viewer and offers no link'), and nw-code-craftsmanship quality axes performant and readable
findings.observation: The Send-test refusal builds a Viewer through caller.viewer(state, door.target.viewer_is_workspace_admin).await, which awaits crate::nav::resolve_is_instance_admin -> state.store.is_instance_admin(user_id), a database read (nav.rs:236-248); it then takes .words and discards .fixes. is_instance_admin only ever feeds ConnectionWords::fixes (Viewer::offers_with_setup), never the sentence, so that read cannot change a byte of this response. The refusal then calls refused_page -> routes.rs::project_answer, which builds caller.nav(state, csrf) and performs the very same read a second time, so this path now costs two authorization reads where the authority says it should cost none. Caller::viewer has exactly one caller, this one, and its own doc comment says 'A page that already holds its nav builds the viewer from that instead, so the offer costs it no extra read' - the page behind this call does hold a nav. Severity medium: no observable behaviour changes (the shipped integrations-wayfinding Send-test rows pass), so this is avoidable work and misleading code rather than a defect in output.
findings.remediation: Read the sentence without the instance-admin fact: either give NoConnectionCause a words-only accessor taking is_workspace_admin and call it here, or build the Viewer from the nav project_answer already resolves and pass it down, so the refusal performs no extra read; then delete Caller::viewer if it has no remaining caller. Re-run the integrations-wayfinding lane (it covers the Send-test Matrix and Slack refusal rows) and cargo test -p foundry-app --lib integrations::no_connection.

findings.observation: viewer.offers(None) is written in five arms. Viewer::offers is 'Vec::from_iter(fix.filter(|_| self.is_workspace_admin))', so with a None argument it returns an empty Vec for every viewer: the call reads as a viewer-dependent decision that cannot depend on the viewer. A reader checking whether K-19, K-2 or a lost connection could ever gain a link has to inline the method to learn that it cannot. Severity low, advice only: behaviour is exactly the shipped one and the no_connection table (4 passed, run by this reviewer) pins every one of those rows to an empty offer list.
findings.remediation: In the arms whose fix is structurally absent, write the empty offer directly (Vec::new(), or a named Viewer::no_offers()/NO_OFFERS), keeping viewer.offers(..) for the arms that actually carry a workspace fix, so the viewer appears only where it decides something.

findings.observation: On the route form the oracle exercises only three of the four viewers: Priya (workspace admin AND instance admin), Lena Park seeded as instance admin (instance admin, not workspace admin) and Lena (neither). The viewer AC 3 names for both doors - a workspace admin who is NOT an instance admin - is read on the workspace integrations page only (Tomas, feature file line 524-531); no scenario puts him, or any workspace-admin-but-not-instance-admin, in front of the new-route form, its preview or its save. Concrete surviving mutation, checked by reading the call site: change crates/foundry-app/src/integrations/handlers/route_form.rs:417 to Viewer::new(self.target.viewer_is_workspace_admin, nav.is_instance_admin || self.target.viewer_is_workspace_admin) and every scenario still passes - Priya (true,true) unchanged, Lena Park (false,true) unchanged, Lena (false,false) unchanged - while Tomas's route form would offer him a /admin/instance/integrations link that answers the uniform not-found page, exactly the dead end AC 3 and KPI-IIS-G2 forbid. The shipped integrations-wayfinding rows cannot catch it either: then_fix_offered's Fix::None branch and workspace_links() only count hrefs starting with /workspace/integrations (support/integrations_wayfinding.rs:222-234), so an extra instance-setup link is invisible there, and Fix::Link asserts one matching link without excluding others. The no_connection words table (4 passed, run by this reviewer) pins NoConnectionCause::words for the ADMIN=(true,false) viewer but not the route form's construction of that Viewer, so production support does not close this gap. Implementation and every executed check pass; the missing observation is the defect.
findings.remediation: Add the missing route-form row to the recorded oracle: either a fourth Examples row / a sibling scenario in which Tomas (workspace admin, not this Foundry's instance admin) opens, previews and saves a new Slack route for Identity Platform and 'the links Tomas is offered read "How to set up Slack"' with 'every link Tomas is offered answers with its page', or the same scenario with any workspace admin for whom no instance_admins row is seeded. The existing steps and support need no change (then_page_links already reads every non-sidebar href, including /admin/instance/integrations). Observe the new row RED against a route_form.rs that ORs the two facts, then GREEN on this candidate.
